rows.description: A young professional asks how much she remembers about others' slips, realises people are mostly self-focused, and gives herself permission to speak imperfectly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young child believes that hoping hard or a special ritual can change the roll of a dice or a match result. Feeling in charge is comforting.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child uses a lucky pen, a special seat, or a fixed routine before matches and exams and thinks it affects results. Missing the routine brings real anxiety.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager thinks that choosing his own lottery number or lucky scratch card gives him better odds. Effort and choice feel like they influence pure chance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult believes skill or a system will beat random outcomes, doubling down after losses. Feeling of control keeps him playing when odds are against him.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A wise person asks which parts of an outcome she truly controls, invests effort there, and accepts the random remainder without superstition or self-blame.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child flipping a coin says tails must come next after five heads. He believes chance has a memory and balances itself out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager believes a team or a card must turn up after a long run, and bets friendly stakes on it. Each independent event has no memory of the last.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult keeps betting because a win is due after a losing streak, and losses grow. Random streaks do not correct themselves on demand.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A friend notices someone betting more after each loss, saying his luck will turn. Kind, direct concern and suggesting help matter more than a lecture on probability.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
